title: Está lloviendo otra vez
blurbEn: A rainy street seen from an office window, and the handful of gerunds that don't follow the rule.
body:
Está lloviendo otra vez.

Desde la ventana de la oficina veo la calle. La gente está corriendo con paraguas, los coches están parando en el semáforo y un hombre está esperando el autobús sin abrigo. Está temblando de frío.

Mi compañero Diego está diciendo algo sobre el proyecto, pero yo no estoy escuchando. Estoy pensando en el fin de semana.

—¿Me estás oyendo? —pregunta.

—Claro —miento.

Diego está sonriendo. Sabe perfectamente que no.
translationEn:
It's raining again.

From the office window I can see the street. People are running with umbrellas, the cars are stopping at the traffic light and a man is waiting for the bus without a coat. He is shivering with cold.

My colleague Diego is saying something about the project, but I am not listening. I am thinking about the weekend.

"Are you listening to me?" he asks.

"Of course," I lie.

Diego is smiling. He knows perfectly well that I'm not.

diciendo.note: The e of 'decir' becomes i. Same change as 'pidiendo' from 'pedir'.

oyendo.note: Another vowel stem, so another y — like 'leyendo'.

perfectamente.note: Adjective plus -mente. You will meet the pattern properly in the next text.

phrases.note: Weather works with this too. Compare 'llueve' — it rains, generally.
The pronoun goes before the whole unit, exactly as with 'he comido'.
